Responses API streaming: text followed by a function call shares output_index 0, message never closed, final output reordered
When a streamed `/v1/responses` turn emits assistant text and then a function call, the event stream reuses one `output_index` for both items, never closes the message, and the final `response.output` lists the items in a different order than they were announced. A strict Responses stream consumer rejects the stream with "duplicate output item" or "terminal response changed output order".
A user of our project hit this on Ollama 0.34.4 and 0.35.1 while running a local model with tools. The same code is still on `main` at 42e911b (`openai/responses.go`):
1. Shared `output_index`. `processTextContent` announces the message at `c.outputIndex` and does not advance it. A later chunk with tool calls goes through `emitFunctionCallEvents`, which announces the first `function_call` at `c.outputIndex + 0`. Both `response.output_item.added` events carry the same index.
2. Message never closed. After the tool calls, `toolCallsSent` is set. `processCompletion` then skips `output_text.done`, `content_part.done` and `output_item.done` for the message that was already opened.
3. Final order differs from the stream. `buildFinalOutput` puts `completedItems` (the function calls) first and appends the message last. The message was announced first, so `response.completed.response.output[i]` no longer matches the item announced at `output_index` i.

| Environment value | `KeepAlive()` | `LoadTimeout()` |

A Gemma 4 12B model created from a GGUF is prompted with the small renderer unless its name contains "12b".
The small renderer drops the empty thought block that Google's chat template emits after the model turn when thinking is off, so the prompt no longer matches the model's own template.
Why it happens. `ollama create` sets `RENDERER gemma4`, and `resolveGemma4Renderer` (`server/renderer_resolution.go`) resolves it in this order:
the model's short name, then its name: `e2b`/`e4b` gives small, `12b`/`26b`/`31b` gives large;
otherwise the parameter count against `gemma4LargeMinParameterCount = 12_000_000_000`;
otherwise small.
Gemma 4 12B GGUFs report 11.9B parameters (`ollama show`), so any name without a size falls through to the count and gets `gemma4-small`.
The official library tag is fine because its name contains "12b".
A user's own model, or a published one under a name like `user/my-gemma`, is not.

Clef / Clef Flash: n_ubatch is forced to n_ctx, so default num_ctx 16384 fails to load (OOM / GGML_ASSERT)
For the Clef decision models, llama-server sets n_batch and n_ubatch equal to n_ctx, even though Ollama passes `-b 512 -ub 512`. The compute buffer therefore grows linearly with num_ctx.
The models ship with `num_ctx 16384` (`ollama show clef-flash --parameters`), which overrides OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH. With that default, the compute buffer is 3.3-3.8 GB and loading fails on every backend I tried:
CPU (0.40.1): `failed to allocate CPU buffer of size 3759030304`
ROCm (0.40.0): `cudaMalloc failed: out of memory` (3328 MiB), although the fit step reports 18.7 GB free and "no changes needed"
Vulkan (0.40.0): `ErrorOutOfDeviceMemory`, buffer 4027498500
clef:27b on ROCm (0.35.1): hard crash, `GGML_ASSERT(ctx->mem_buffer != NULL) failed`, exit 0xc0000409
Workaround: a derived model with `PARAMETER num_ctx 4096`. Then n_ubatch = 4096, the compute buffer is ~736 MiB, and clef-flash runs fine on 0.40.1 (1.2-2.6 s per request on a Radeon 890M).
Expected behavior
Either respect `-ub 512` for decision models, or account for the n_ubatch-sized compute buffer in the memory fit and reduce context automatically instead of failing. A lower default num_ctx for Clef would also help, since decision requests are usually short.

The architecture (as implemented by this proposal)
KailA reuses standard transformer building blocks with two additions:

Router-gated SwiGLU FFN: a router gates the gate branch before the elementwise product with the up branch.
RMSNorm at attention/FFN/output; tied input/output embeddings; RoPE (NORM variant).

[Feature Proposal]: Portable CLI Wrappers (ollama.bat/ollama.sh) for Centralized Configuration & Daemon Control
🚀 Feature Proposal: Cross-Platform CLI Wrappers (`ollama.bat` & `ollama.sh`)
Summary
Configuring Ollama's runtime environment (`OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION`, context lengths, VRAM/GPU allocation, logging levels) currently requires either setting persistent OS-level environment variables or chaining them before inline CLI commands. Managing daemon lifecycles (`start`, `stop`, `restart`) across operating systems often requires manual task termination (`taskkill`, `pkill`).
This proposal introduces two zero-dependency management wrappers:
`ollama.bat` (Windows Command Prompt)
`ollama.sh` (Linux / macOS / POSIX Bash)
---
Key Capabilities
1. Centralized Configuration: Tune environment variables (`OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH`, `OLLAMA_FLASH_ATTENTION`, `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE`, timeouts, hardware flags) directly in the script header.
2. Background Daemon Management: Run the server as a detached background process (`start /b` on Windows, `nohup ... &` on Unix).
3. Guardrails & Health Checks: Checks whether the daemon is running before forwarding client commands (`run`, `pull`, `ps`), and prevents duplicate instances on `start`.
4. Bulk Maintenance (`update all`): Iterates over all downloaded local models and runs `ollama pull` for each one automatically.
5. Transparent Pass-Through: Forwards arguments and flags cleanly to the base `ollama` binary.
---
Command Comparison
| Operation | Default Ollama CLI | Wrapper Script |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Start Daemon | `ollama serve` *(blocks shell)* |

The problem
Ollama binds to loopback by default, but a lot of people set `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` so another machine, a container, a phone or Open WebUI can reach it. From that point the API is unauthenticated and open to anyone who can route to the port. `allowedHostsMiddleware` only covers DNS rebinding through the `Host` header, it doesn't decide who gets to connect.
Concrete cases:
A home-lab or office box with `OLLAMA_HOST=0.0.0.0` and a port forward, or a cloud VM with the port open in the security group. Scanners find it, and then anyone can run models on the owner's GPU, pull or delete models, or hammer `/api/generate` until `OLLAMA_MAX_QUEUE` fills and real users are starved.
A shared lab or LAN where I want one subnet allowed and nothing else, without writing firewall rules on every machine.
One script stuck in a loop that should be throttled per client instead of exhausting the queue for everyone.
Authentication is the real fix (#12476, #14003) and this is not a replacement for it. IP policy, bans and per-client budgets are orthogonal to credentials, so they stay useful after auth lands.

Integer `seed` above 2^53 loses precision (options decoded as float64), so distinct seeds give identical output
Integer options in `options` are decoded from JSON as `float64` before they are converted to `int`. A `seed` larger than 2^53 is rounded to the nearest representable double. So different seeds can become the same effective seed, and the request still succeeds silently.
We found this because a repeated-sampling experiment came back with byte-identical outputs on every repeat. Each repeat used a consecutive 64-bit seed at temperature 0.7. All three seeds in each group rounded to the same value:
6887878990344476218 -> 6887878990344476672
6887878990344476219 -> 6887878990344476672
6887878990344476220 -> 6887878990344476672
This happened in 70 of 70 groups (211 requests). From the client side it looks exactly like the seed being ignored.

install.sh calling sudo immediately after download forces user to be present at download completion
`install.sh` downloads ollamaxxx.tar.zst and uses sudo to extract the file. If user is not present the sudo password prompt will timeout.
On slower connections it's practical to leave the install unattended while the download completes. However if sudo times out, the installer prints a success message and exits.
Reattempting causes the download to start all over again.

Scheduler stalls: runner marked "expire immediately" for eviction never unloads while other clients keep using it (keep_alive overrides the eviction)
What is the issue?
When a new model needs VRAM and Ollama decides to evict an already-loaded model,
the scheduler marks that runner as *"resetting model to expire immediately to make
room"* and waits for it to unload. But if other clients keep sending requests to the
runner being evicted (each with a non-zero `keep_alive`), every new request
overwrites the "expire immediately" duration with its own `keep_alive`. When the
runner becomes idle (`refCount=0`), the scheduler then logs *"runner with non-zero
duration has gone idle, adding timer"* instead of unloading it.
As long as those clients keep the runner busy, the eviction never completes:
the request for the new model waits forever (until the client times out), and since
the scheduler is blocked in *"waiting for pending requests to complete and unload to
occur"*, no other model can be loaded either. Requests to the already-loaded model
keep working, so from the outside Ollama looks alive.
